newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger says no loss of NZ fiscal discipline.
newsitem.headline: Bolger says no loss of NZ fiscal discipline.

text.p: The New Zealand coalition government's expenditure plans should not be characterised as a loss of discipline, Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Tuesday.

Bolger, speaking at the New Zealand Investment Conference, repeated that over the 1997/8 year, new spending had been limited to a maximum of NZ$950 million, which was lower than the maximum specified in last December's coalition agreement between his conservative National Party and NZ First.
"Some of you will be concerned about the implications of this spending on the dollar and for interest rates. The government is acutely aware of these concerns," Bolger said.
"But it important to realise that the government's 1997/8 operating balance is now projected to be higher than forecast before the coalition agreement was put together," he said.
"The coalition government's new expenditure plans should not be characterised as a loss of discipline. Our resolve to reduce our debt and to retain healthy budget surpluses remains," Bolger said.
Bolger noted that New Zealand remained one of only three OECD countries not struggling to balance its budget.
But the government was equally committed to getting the best return from its increased investment "in our human capital".
On trade, Bolger said the government would continue to the systematic and progressive reduction of remaining barriers to imports and reducing the obstacles for exporters.
